lines: {target}? Green stalks can hide quick trouble. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Bamboo Jungle, tell them. Keep a path cut behind you. I'll be at the bell.
Bamboo crowds the eye and the feet. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Bamboo Jungle is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Bamboo Jungle as a green wall that rustles like whispers. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
If I could still reach the last clearing outside the bamboo, I would call myself only partly lost. That is better than usual.
If I noticed a spider between the stalks, I would give it all the room it wanted and perhaps extra.
I would ask what heavy rain meant for the trip. Guessing at conditions has gone badly before.
If anyone got separated at Bamboo Jungle, I would stay near the last clearing outside the bamboo and not improve the plan.
Bamboo Jungle sounds like a place where my best idea would arrive shortly after I left.
At Bamboo Jungle, I would tie everything twice. Loose laces have excellent timing.
Bringing food, shears, and a compass would make Bamboo Jungle less foolish. I would still provide foolishness on my own.
If I spotted something unusual at Bamboo Jungle, I would point first and move much later.
Seeing the tall bamboo closing over the trail would make our village paths seem wonderfully boring. I like boring paths.
A map of Bamboo Jungle would help, especially with a large drawing of the last clearing outside the bamboo.
At Bamboo Jungle, a short rest near the last clearing outside the bamboo might prevent a very long mistake.
The best part of Bamboo Jungle could be telling the story from my own bed.
If told not to pull something at Bamboo Jungle, I would stand too far away to hear it as a challenge.
At Bamboo Jungle, fresh air would count as a landmark even if the map disagreed.
If the group split at Bamboo Jungle, I would choose the half containing the person with the map.
{target}? Leaves crowd close enough to hide anything. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Jungle, tell them. Cut a path and remember which vines you passed. I will be at the bell.
The green is loud even when nothing moves. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Jungle is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Jungle as a hot forest that keeps secrets well. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Darkness makes every route feel secret. I already forget enough things in daylight.
At Jungle, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with a drop hidden by leaves, I would leave the loot. I hope.
I would warn people about a spider in the vines and let someone else add dramatic noises.
I would not decide that leaves moving above the trail meant no trouble at Jungle without asking someone else.
If I noticed a spider in the vines, I would give it all the room it wanted and perhaps extra.
I am poor at judging distance, especially when something interesting is at the other end.
Good light might help me avoid a drop hidden by leaves. That is worth the extra torches.
If the plan went wrong, the last clear patch of sky should be where it became simple again.
At Jungle, I would keep the slowest traveler beside me. There is a fair chance that traveler is me.
Slow steps near vines and jungle wood sound dull. Dull steps tend to reach home.
Jungle might change quickly under heavy rain. I would keep the route home clear.
I would wave at Jungle when leaving. I wave at places sometimes. They rarely wave back.
I know the sound people make when I miss a sign. I hope not to hear it while dealing with a drop hidden by leaves.
A strange smell near the vines and thick leaves would send me back toward the last clear patch of sky.
Food would not solve a drop hidden by leaves, but being hungry might make it worse.
{target}? Mud holds boots longer than plans. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Mangrove Swamp, tell them. Step on roots and keep slime in mind. I will be at the bell.
Thick roots make every hurry foolish. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Mangrove Swamp is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Mangrove Swamp as muddy water with a grip on your ankles. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Stories never mention frogs calling across the water in enough detail. They leave out useful things like that.
I would take deep mud hiding the bottom seriously, even if I had just said something very unserious.
If swamp mist made the firm bank behind the mangroves hard to see, finding it again would feel wonderful.
A good memory of Mangrove Swamp weighs less than a full pack and cannot fall on my foot.
Is Mangrove Swamp worth the walk? That depends on how much you enjoy walking back.
If I spotted something unusual at Mangrove Swamp, I would point first and move much later.
I would find the firm bank behind the mangroves before going farther. I lose directions more often than chalk.
I would keep my socks dry if Mangrove Swamp allowed it. This feels ambitious already.
If anyone got separated at Mangrove Swamp, I would stay near the firm bank behind the mangroves and not improve the plan.
Food would not solve deep mud hiding the bottom, but being hungry might make it worse.
The village has fewer surprises than Mangrove Swamp. This is one of its finest qualities.
Nothing found at Mangrove Swamp would be worth losing sight of the firm bank behind the mangroves.
My fingers do not need to investigate mangrove wood. My eyes can file the report.
I would carry more light to Mangrove Swamp than seemed necessary. Necessary moves after sunset.
I would be pleased to see familiar roofs after the muddy water between mangrove roots. I might even say so.
{target}? Thin jungle still keeps thick surprises. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Sparse Jungle, tell them. Don't trust open patches too quickly. I will be at the bell.
Vines and shadows take turns hiding things. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Sparse Jungle is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Sparse Jungle as green country pretending to be easier than it is. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
Sparse Jungle might look close from the last clear rise above the trees. Places lie about distance when I am tired.
I would ask what heavy rain meant for the trip. Guessing at conditions has gone badly before.
If anyone got separated at Sparse Jungle, I would stay near the last clear rise above the trees and not improve the plan.
I would save torches for the return from Sparse Jungle. The return always gets the leftovers.
I ask too many questions around strange places. At least questions do not make a drop hidden by low leaves worse.
I would return before people had to wonder where I wandered. They do enough of that.
If the air changed around Sparse Jungle, I would mention it before everyone blamed my lunch.
At Sparse Jungle, I would keep my hands off anything that clicked, hissed, glowed, or looked offended.
Someone should remind me that the last clear rise above the trees is for getting home, not just admiring.
Sparse Jungle may be pleasant. It also may have heard me say that and taken it personally.
I have packed for trips before. This time I would remember food, torches, and a compass before a spoon.
At Sparse Jungle, if carrying loot made it harder to deal with a drop hidden by low leaves, I would leave the loot. I hope.
I would bring news home if a spider in the vines blocked the route. Quickly and with many hand gestures.
My feet should vote before I walk through the widely spaced jungle trees and vines. They usually vote for home.
I would eat before reaching Sparse Jungle. Hungry me makes decisions that ordinary me questions.
{target}? Mud and water both remember footsteps. I would stay close enough to hear the bell.
If anyone heads for Swamp, tell them. Watch slimes, witches, and the slow ground. I will be at the bell.
Fog makes close things feel far. I'll remember that from near the bell.
Swamp is no small story. Running the wrong way is still running.
I will remember Swamp as wet land that grabs at ankles and plans. I will stay where I can hear the bell.
If my legs started wobbling near the muddy water between roots, I would listen to them for once.
If everyone became grumpy at Swamp, I would check the food before blaming the destination.
I would tell the group before stepping away. Waving from far off is not the same thing.
The far side of the muddy water between roots can stay far. I need not stand on every side of everything.
Conditions like heavy rain could change the whole trip to Swamp. I would rather notice early.
Before leaving for Swamp, I would check twice that I had food, a boat, and dry socks. Then I would ask someone else.
Swamp would make me curious. It would also make me glad someone else knows when to stop.
Feeling brave near a slime beyond the reeds would not make me walk closer. I can be brave over here.
At Swamp, deep mud hiding the bottom could ruin a good walk. I am already capable of doing that myself.
At Swamp, even village chores sound good. None of them involve deep mud hiding the bottom.
If the air changed around Swamp, I would mention it before everyone blamed my lunch.
Treasure at Swamp would still be there after I checked the way home. If not, perhaps it had plans.
Before exploring the muddy water between roots, I would make everyone agree to meet at the firm bank behind the roots.
I might bring back a little mud and lily pads, as long as taking it caused no trouble.
Strange places dislike idle hands. I can carry the food bag and keep mine busy.
